D003_l001.question:
A 48-year-old married male, working as a factory supervisor, presents with a 2-year and 2-month history of persistent behavioral and cognitive symptoms causing marked functional impairment in occupational and interpersonal domains. The patient reports longstanding difficulties with sustained attention, frequently failing to complete工作任务 despite understanding expectations and instructions. He struggles with organizing daily tasks and responsibilities, leading to inefficiencies at work and increased supervision needs. 

Clinically significant hyperactivity and impulsivity are endorsed. The patient describes habitual fidgeting, including hand tapping and foot movements while seated, and frequently leaves his seat in meetings or structured settings. He reports a persistent internal sense of restlessness, though overt running or climbing is absent. Impulsivity manifests as frequent interruptions during conversations and a consistent pattern of blurting responses before questions are fully asked, as well as marked difficulty waiting for his turn during social or work-related interactions.

Per patient report, several of these behaviors were present before age 12, particularly in school settings, though not formally evaluated. The factory supervisor role, which demands sustained focus and structured planning, has become increasingly challenging. Marital strain is noted but has existed independently for several years prior to symptom escalation, with no direct temporal link to current presentation. Symptoms are present across multiple settings and are not attributable to another psychiatric or medical condition.

    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
